chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Abd Al-Karim ibn Amr has been transmitted by me from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with them both), from Sad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr Al-Bazanti, from Abd Al-Karim ibn Amr Al-Khathami, whose title was Karram.

key_terms.أحمد بن محمد بن أبي نصر البزنطي: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr Al-Bazanti, a key link in the chain
key_terms.الخثعمي: Al-Khathami, referring to the tribe of the narrator
key_terms.عبد الكريم بن عمرو: Abd Al-Karim ibn Amr, a prominent narrator
key_terms.كرام: Karram, the kunya or title of the narrator

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator Abd Al-Karim ibn Amr and how is his chain of transmission verified in Al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous verification of the *isnad* for Abd Al-Karim ibn Amr, a key narrator in Kufan hadith circles. By tracing the chain through his father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, al-Saduq underscores the reliability of the transmission and the scholarly rigor applied to validating the authority of these narrations in Shia jurisprudence.
